title: A Soroban transaction fails txNO_ACCOUNT at apply and its fee is never refunded
pattern: Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger merges the source account after its fee was charged, so this Soroban transaction fails with txNO_ACCOUNT. The refund has nowhere to go: there is no post-apply fee change and no refund event, and fee_charged is the full declared maximum (TransactionFrame.cpp:998-1001). Readers that compute the fee as charge minus refund, or expect a refund for every Soroban transaction, get it wrong.

hazards.placement: TransactionResult.txNO_ACCOUNT in a closed ledger: source merged earlier in the ledger
Soroban fee source merged before the refund: fee_charged is the full maximum, no refund change or event

facts.says: The transaction fails with tx_no_account although it was valid when submitted.
The transaction that caused it is in the same ledger.
The sequence number is not consumed: no change before apply.
No operation was applied: the operation meta is empty.
The transaction source is the account changed earlier in the ledger.
No refund: there is no post-apply fee processing.
fee_charged is the full declared maximum: 100 stroops inclusion plus the whole 100,000,000-stroop resource fee.
